messages:
ashley: :rotating_light: Customer ACME (acct: acme-prod) reporting sudden p99 spikes and intermittent GPU OOMs on completions route. Started ~2026-03-16T16:10Z. p95 up from ~120ms to ~1.2s, p99 up to 6s. They see errors: "cuda out of memory" followed by big latency tail.

ashley: quick summary metrics we grabbed:
```
node=gpu-rt-45 mem_total=48GB mem_used=46.3GB kv_cache_bytes=1.18GB kv_entries=342k active_allocations=~24k
node=gpu-rt-46 mem_total=48GB mem_used=47.1GB kv_cache_bytes=1.25GB kv_entries=368k
route=completions-prod-v3 model=redwood/7b-v1-qa-quant
qps spike ~250 -> 900 for tenant acme-prod
```

sam: on it — can you confirm if there was a recent model or runtime rollout? any cfg changes for kv sizing or allocator? also paste last 5 lines of runtime stderr from gpu-rt-45 if you have them.

ashley: we rolled model 2026-03-16 15:55 UTC (7b-v1-qa-quant with new kv-prefetch). No other infra rollouts. stderr snippet: 
```
[16:09:52] runtime: kv_cache resize from 512MB -> 1024MB
[16:10:03] runtime: allocation failure: alloc_bytes=134217728 stack=(...)
[16:10:03] runtime: cuda error: out of memory
[16:10:03] runtime: falling back to slower path, increasing latency
```

maria: I see OOM kill logs on gpu-rt-45 and gpu-rt-46 in our observability. There are repeated small alloc/free churns and kv size steadily grows per-tenant (acme-prod) even when requests are idle — looks like KV growth leak.

maria: metrics endpoint for node (sample): `GET https://rt-metrics.internal/nodes/gpu-rt-45/heap_heatmap` -> returns hot slab usage around 56MB slabs, high fragmentation ratio 0.64.

kai: initial triage notes: this reads as KV growth + allocator fragmentation causing usable GPU memory to drop and then OOM on large allocations -> large tail latency as runtime falls back to slower CPU path. Immediate mitigations (run ASAP):
1) Apply a per-tenant KV soft cap for acme-prod: `kv_cache.max_bytes=200MB` via control-plane (will trigger eviction).
2) Temporarily throttle concurrency for acme-prod to 6 concurrent requests.
3) Route acme-prod to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint: `redwood/7b-v1-qa-quant-smallkv` (quick canary).
4) For affected nodes, trigger slab compaction job (non-disruptive request): `POST /admin/nodes/gpu-rt-45/actions/compact?type=kv` — this forces offline compaction/eviction.

kai: commands (control plane):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme-prod/config -d '{"kv_cache.max_bytes": 209715200}'
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme-prod/actions/throttle -d '{"concurrency":6}'
```

sam: agree with those. Additional quick runtime-level tweak: set env `ALLOCATOR_SLAB_TARGET=32MB` on a single affected node and roll it for verification (reduces fragmentation at cost of some metadata overhead). Also push a patched allocator (v2.1) to a single canary host that fixes a known leak on kv eviction.

ashley: Ashley -> I've applied tenant kv cap and throttle (control-plane accepted). I also routed ~10% of acme traffic to the smallkv model. Observability: acme-prod p99 down to ~2.1s after throttle, node mem_used slowly decreasing. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollout started: allocator-v2.1 -> canary gpu-rt-49 at 16:34 UTC.

maria: after compaction on gpu-rt-45 we saw immediate ~800MB reclaimed and fragmentation ratio drop to ~0.36. No more OOM kills in last 7m on that host. Still monitoring other hosts.

kai: follow-up actions for next 24h:
- Schedule full canary batch for allocator-v2.1 (monitor kv retention and leak counter).
- Add per-tenant kv eviction metrics and alert when kv_bytes grows > 85% of cap for 10m.
- Add automated fallback routing rule: if runtime OOM rate > 0.5% for a node for 5m then migrate affected tenants to smallkv variant or dedicated nodes.
- Work on long-term fix: identify root cause of kv growth (suspect prefetch bug in new model code) — repro locally with generator script.

sam: repro steps we used to reproduce locally (throttled load generator):
```
python load_gen.py --route completions-prod-v3 --model redwood/7b-v1-qa-quant --qps 400 --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 40 --duration 10m
# watch /metrics for kv_entries and fragmentation
```

ashley: Customer notified and on a call with support and eng. They've accepted temporary throttling and smallkv routing while we stabilize. Putting incident in monitoring with severity: high.

kai: assigning action owners: ashley (customer comms), sam (canary allocator rollout + repro), kai (runtime mitigations + fallback rule), maria (monitoring alerts). Will post a short postmortem after stable.

ashley: thanks all — will update ACME and close escalation when p99 < 500ms and no OOMs for 2 hours.
